steps.intent: Panama’s objective is to renew BINUH with a crisis-responsive, Haitian-led mandate that reinforces protection of civilians, humanitarian access, sanctions implementation and coordination with the MSS while preserving Council unity. The main difficulties will be language on a possible future UN mission and on the role of BINUH in supporting gang-dismantling efforts, where China and Russia may seek to avoid anything that looks like authorization for expanded UN involvement and where the United States will push for stronger security and accountability provisions.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports extending BINUH and welcomes the draft's focus on a Haitian-led political process. We ask that national ownership be made explicit in the operational paragraphs, that support to the MSS be framed by full respect for Haiti's sovereignty and international law, and that any future UN mission be considered only with Haiti's consent and clear benchmarks.
messages.China: China supports the extension of BINUH’s mandate and stresses that the Council’s action must remain Haitian-led and respect Haiti’s sovereignty. We request the above changes to make clear that BINUH’s work, including any future transition, is at the request of the Government of Haiti, and to strengthen implementation of the arms embargo, which remains a key gap in the current response. China is ready to work constructively with the penholders.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the extension of BINUH and welcomes Panama's balanced draft. We ask for targeted strengthening on women's full, equal and meaningful participation in the political process, public human rights reporting and follow-up on impunity, and conditions-based transition language that preserves protection of civilians and human rights monitoring. We would also like climate-related security risks reflected in reporting.
messages.France: France supports the renewal of BINUH and thanks Panama and the United States for the draft. We seek limited adjustments: the strategic assessment should not prejudge a transition and should be conditions-based and Haitian-owned; the Council should also call clearly for full implementation of the 2752 sanctions and arms embargo. We would also like the human rights language to include conflict-related sexual violence and accountability.
messages.Greece: Greece welcomes the draft and supports the renewal of BINUH’s mandate. We would like the text to include an explicit humanitarian safeguard for the sanctions regime, stronger regional cooperation against illicit arms trafficking by sea, land and air, and more specific reporting on sexual and gender-based violence and grave violations against children. Greece can support the text with these amendments.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the renewal of BINUH and welcomes the draft’s focus on a Haitian-led political process, protection of civilians, accountability and sanctions implementation. We ask the penholders to strengthen the CARICOM link in OP1(a), to include predictable, sustainable and adequate funding language for the MSS in OP5, including consideration of assessed contributions, and to clarify in OP6 that the strategic assessment will consult CARICOM and will not prejudge any future UN mission. These changes would align the text with the A3+ and CARICOM positions and help secure consensus.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the renewal of BINUH's mandate and thanks Panama for a balanced draft. We ask that OP2 explicitly include poverty, socio-economic inequality and underdevelopment among root causes, and that OP1(c) confirm sanctions implementation is consistent with resolution 2664 (2022) and preserves humanitarian exemptions and fair delisting procedures. We also seek language in OP6 that any strategic assessment and possible transition fully respect Haiti's sovereignty, national ownership and the views of its Government.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports renewing BINUH's mandate and the draft's overall balance. Drawing on our statement on resolution 2751 (2024), we ask that OP5 emphasize predictable, sustained and adequate support for the MSS mission and burden-sharing, and that OP6 include the MSS mission's sustainability in the Secretary-General's strategic assessment. This will help ensure that any future transition is realistic and grounded in strengthened Haitian and multinational security capacity.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the extension of BINUH's mandate, but the text must address the external sources of the arms fuelling gang violence, including the flow of American weapons, and must not prejudge a transition to a future UN mission while the situation remains fragile. We also ask that the mandate be explicitly anchored in Haiti's sovereignty and national ownership. These changes are necessary for us to be able to support the draft.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the extension of BINUH and the Haitian-led political process outlined in this draft. We would like the Council to make operative the call for full implementation of the arms embargo and regional border cooperation, given the grave threat posed by illicit arms flows. We also ask that the strategic assessment consult Haitian civil society, including women and youth, and that support for the MSS be framed as predictable and sustainable. We are flexible on wording but consider these points important for an effective and accountable mandate.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia welcomes the comprehensive draft and supports the renewal of BINUH's mandate. We ask the penholder to strengthen safeguards that security responses are protection-of-civilians-oriented and fully compliant with international law, and to reinforce accountability for grave violations. We would also welcome explicit human rights due diligence language for the MSS mission.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the renewal of BINUH and the draft’s strong condemnation of gang violence. We would like the text to reflect the need for predictable and sustainable support for the MSS, including exploring UN assessed contributions, consistent with the Council’s support for African-led peace operations. We also ask for explicit recognition of African Union and CARICOM contributions and affirmation that any future transition is Haitian-led and consensual.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes this draft and supports the extension of BINUH's mandate. We would like the text to reflect the call to consider the transformation of the MSS mission, as we have previously said, and to make clear that the MSS and all security providers must meet the highest international standards, including human rights due diligence. We also suggest strengthening reporting on implementation of the arms embargo and sanctions regime.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the draft as a strong basis for renewing BINUH and urges swift adoption. We request a new operative paragraph calling on all Member States to fully implement the Haiti sanctions regime, and targeted additions to strengthen support for the MSS and fulfillment of existing pledges.

replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: generic arms-exporting States language and no-prejudice transition language included; naming the United States omitted.
replies.Sierra Leone: accepted: sanctions implementation, regional cooperation, civil-society consultation and predictable support included.
replies.Slovenia: accepted: protection-of-civilians orientation, accountability and HRDD language included.

It should retain P5 support or acquiescence and well above the nine-vote threshold.

Somalia.change: Replace “consider all available options to ensure predictable and sustainable funding for the MSS mission” with “consider all available options, including United Nations assessed contributions, to ensure predictable and sustainable funding for the MSS mission, in line with relevant Council decisions”

messages.Algeria: Algeria welcomes the integration of its previous requests, particularly the reaffirmation of Haitian-led and Haitian-owned processes, sovereignty, IHL/IHRL safeguards, and conditions-based, consensual transition language. The text strikes an appropriate balance in supporting BINUH and the MSS while respecting Haiti’s sovereignty and the primary responsibility of its authorities. Algeria therefore supports the draft as it stands and will vote in favour.
messages.China: China supports the current text and has no further changes to propose. We welcome the incorporation of language affirming Haiti’s sovereignty and the request-based nature of BINUH’s work, as well as the strengthened arms-embargo implementation and the requirement for a Haitian request and Council decision for any transition. We call on all partners to ensure predictable funding for the MSS mission and full implementation of the sanctions regime, and we are ready to vote in favour.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the current text and welcomes the incorporation of our earlier requests on participation, public reporting and impunity, conditions-based transition, protection of civilians and climate-related risks. We thank the penholder for the inclusive consultations and are ready to vote in favour of the draft as it stands.
messages.France: France welcomes revision 1 and supports the text as it stands. Our key concerns on a conditions-based phased transition, full implementation of the sanctions and arms embargo, and conflict-related sexual violence and impunity language have been incorporated. France encourages the Council to remain united and to adopt the resolution without further delay.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the revised draft and welcomes the incorporation of our earlier requests on humanitarian safeguards, maritime and border controls, and disaggregated reporting. We believe the text appropriately renews BINUH’s mandate, reinforces the arms embargo and conditions support to the MSS mission on full compliance with international humanitarian and human rights law, including due diligence. Greece can support the text as presented and encourages full implementation, continued attention to protection of civilians and accountability, and respect for Haitian ownership and sovereignty.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the revised text and thanks Panama and the United States for incorporating CARICOM coordination and the no-prejudice language. We welcome the reference to considering all available options for predictable and sustainable MSS funding and understand the need to preserve consensus by not specifying assessed contributions. We will vote in favour and encourage continued attention to sustained, predictable support for the MSS and Haitian ownership.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the revised draft and will vote in favour. We appreciate the penholder's incorporation of our concerns on root causes, humanitarian exemptions consistent with resolution 2664 (2022), and Haiti's sovereignty and national ownership. We encourage the Council to maintain focus on full implementation of the arms embargo and on predictable, coordinated support for the MSS mission and Haitian national institutions.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the current text as revised. We appreciate the incorporation of predictable voluntary financing, burden-sharing and MSS sustainability, which are essential for the Mission’s effectiveness. We encourage all Council members to unite behind the draft and focus on implementation, including protection of civilians, sanctions enforcement and a Haitian-led political process.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the current text and is ready to vote in favour. We welcome the inclusion of language on arms-exporting States and the explicit no-prejudice clause regarding any future transition. We expect all Member States, especially those responsible for the bulk of illicit arms flows, to take effective measures to implement the embargo. We will address the issue of American weapons in our explanation of vote.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the revised draft and commends the penholder for incorporating our proposals on sanctions implementation, regional cooperation, civil-society consultation and predictable support. We urge the Council to speak with one voice and to ensure full implementation of the arms embargo, humanitarian exemptions and human rights due diligence. Sierra Leone will vote in favour if the text is put to the vote.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the current text as a balanced and comprehensive renewal of BINUH's mandate. We welcome the incorporation of our prior requests on a protection-of-civilians-oriented approach, accountability, and human rights due diligence. We encourage full implementation of the text and remain committed to working with the Council on Haiti.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the revised draft and appreciates the inclusion of African Union/CARICOM recognition and consensual transition language. We continue to believe predictable, sustainable funding is essential for the MSS mission’s effectiveness and for African contributions, so OP7 should explicitly include consideration of United Nations assessed contributions. This is an important request, but Somalia can join consensus if the final text remains balanced.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks Panama and the United States for their leadership and welcomes the revisions reflecting our priorities on the transformation of the MSS mission, human rights due diligence and accountability, and reporting on the arms embargo and sanctions regime. We support the current text as a balanced basis for Council unity and the renewal of BINUH’s mandate. We encourage all members to join consensus and support swift adoption.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the revised draft and appreciates Panama's incorporation of our earlier suggestions on sanctions implementation and MSS funding. We urge all Council members to join consensus and adopt the text promptly so BINUH and the MSS can continue their vital work. We stress the need for full implementation of the arms embargo and timely fulfillment of MSS pledges.

replies.Somalia: partially accepted: added 'in line with relevant Council decisions' but did not include explicit assessed contributions, preserving consensus and avoiding P5 objections

reasons.Algeria: Algeria had already signalled support and the draft upholds Haitian sovereignty, UN coordination, humanitarian access and sanctions implementation consistent with Algeria’s positions. Voting in favour reflects its established support for BINUH and Haitian-led political and security efforts.
reasons.China: China has supported previous consensus renewals of BINUH and the Haiti sanctions/MSS framework, and this draft preserves Haitian sovereignty, national ownership, and Council oversight over any future transition. No red line requires abstention or a pre-vote explanation.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark consistently supports BINUH, human rights, humanitarian access, and Haitian-led solutions; the draft aligns with these priorities and Denmark indicated support with no changes requested.
reasons.France: France has consistently supported BINUH, the MSS mission and the Haiti sanctions regime, and the draft is aligned with its stated policy. No French concerns were raised in the last negotiation round.
reasons.Greece: Greece has consistently supported UN mandates on Haiti and the balanced draft reflects its priorities on sovereignty, humanitarian access, human rights, and multilateral coordination. There are no Greek red lines that would require abstention or opposition.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana supports the draft’s renewal of BINUH, its Haitian-led political focus, CARICOM coordination, and emphasis on sanctions and MSS support. No concerns required requesting changes or explaining the vote before the vote.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan's record shows consistent support for UN action on Haiti, and it had already signalled support for the draft with no changes requested. The resolution aligns with Pakistan's emphasis on sovereignty, Haitian ownership, humanitarian access and multilateral support.
reasons.Panama: Panama is the penholder and co-sponsor of the draft with the United States, so it would vote in favour. It would speak before the vote to rally Council unity while emphasizing sovereignty, protection of civilians, and Haitian-led political and security efforts.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported renewing BINUH and the MSS, and it requested no changes in the last negotiation round. A positive vote with a supportive explanation aligns with its established emphasis on Haitian ownership, predictable security support, accountability, and humanitarian access.
reasons.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation had already signalled support and has consistently voted for BINUH/MSS rollovers; its statement records its standard caveats on sovereignty, arms trafficking, humanitarian exemptions and Council prerogatives. The draft poses no fundamental objection, so Russia votes yes.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone has consistently supported previous Haiti resolutions and was recorded as supporting this draft without changes. Voting in favour aligns with its multilateralist posture, respect for sovereignty, and emphasis on humanitarian access and regional peace efforts.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia had already indicated support and made no changes to the draft; as an elected member prioritising human rights, protection of civilians and multilateral coordination, it would vote in favour while explaining those priorities.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia had requested explicit assessed contributions for predictable MSS funding, but the penholder only partially accepted it. Given Somalia’s support for BINUH, the MSS mission, and Council unity on Haiti, it votes yes while explaining its remaining concern.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports renewing BINUH’s mandate, strengthening implementation of the arms embargo and sanctions, and backing a Haitian-led political process; it had no outstanding requests and would likely explain its vote after adoption rather than before.
reasons.United States of America: The United States co-sponsored the draft and has consistently supported renewing BINUH, backing the MSS mission, and strengthening Haiti sanctions and arms embargo implementation. The text aligns with US policy and the delegation’s stated position in the final negotiation round.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour. We support the extension of BINUH because the crisis in Haiti requires a sustained, coordinated and Haitian-led response. We reaffirm Haiti’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity and stress that international support must be at the request of and in close consultation with the Government of Haiti. We welcome the emphasis on political facilitation, protection of civilians, humanitarian access, accountability and the full participation of women, youth and civil society. We also underline the need for full implementation of the arms embargo and sanctions, including preventing illicit arms flows, while preserving humanitarian exemptions. Algeria encourages stronger coordination with CARICOM and the African Union and supports predictable support for the MSS mission consistent with international law and human rights due diligence.
before.Denmark: Denmark thanks Panama and the United States for the draft and welcomes the broad support it has received. We vote in favour. Denmark strongly supports the extension of BINUH’s mandate and a Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process, including preparations for credible, inclusive and fair elections with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society. We underscore the need for full implementation of the arms embargo and sanctions, unhindered humanitarian access, accountability for serious violations, and robust human rights due diligence for all security providers. Denmark also stresses the importance of predictable and sustainable support for the MSS mission and of a conditions-based strategic assessment of the United Nations presence, with clear benchmarks and continued protection of civilians in close partnership with Haiti and regional partners.
before.France: La France votera en faveur du projet de résolution. La prorogation du mandat de la BINUH est essentielle pour soutenir la transition politique, la protection des civils et la mise en œuvre du régime de sanctions. Nous appelons tous les acteurs haïtiens à œuvrer à la tenue d’élections crédibles et à la restauration des institutions démocratiques, et nous réaffirmons notre plein appui à la souveraineté, à l’indépendance et à l’intégrité territoriale d’Haïti.
before.Greece: Greece will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the extension of BINUH’s mandate and a coordinated, Haitian-led response to the crisis, with full respect for Haiti’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. We stress the importance of protecting civilians, ensuring safe and unhindered humanitarian access, strengthening implementation of the arms embargo, and maintaining robust human rights due diligence and accountability in all security support.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the extension of BINUH’s mandate and reiterate our strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and unity of Haiti. Pakistan supports a Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process, the protection of civilians, unhindered humanitarian access, accountability for grave violations, and effective implementation of the arms embargo and sanctions regime. We also stress the need for predictable and sustained support for the Multinational Security Support mission, with full respect for international law and Haitian national ownership, while addressing the root causes of insecurity and underdevelopment. Pakistan remains committed to supporting the people of Haiti in restoring stability, democracy and development.
before.Panama: Panama votes in favour of the draft resolution it has submitted together with the United States. The situation in Haiti demands Council unity and urgent, sustained action. Panama stresses that international support must be Haitian-led and Haitian-owned, fully respect Haiti’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, and prioritize the protection of civilians, humanitarian access, accountability, and the fight against impunity and arms trafficking. We call on all Member States to support BINUH, the MSS mission and the sanctions regime, and to advance a credible political process leading to elections and the restoration of democratic institutions. Panama remains committed to the people of Haiti and to the Council’s responsibility to maintain international peace and security.
before.Republic of Korea:
The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of this important draft resolution. We thank Panama and the United States for their efforts to guide the Council towards a balanced and credible text.

The renewal of BINUH’s mandate is essential to sustaining the United Nations’ good offices and coordinated support for a Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process, including preparations for credible elections and the restoration of democratic institutions. At the same time, the worsening security and humanitarian situation demands that the Council remain firm on protecting civilians, ensuring safe and unhindered humanitarian access, strengthening the arms embargo, and holding perpetrators of violence accountable.

We underscore that international support must be delivered in full respect for Haiti’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity. The Republic of Korea also stresses the need for predictable and sustainable support to the Multinational Security Support mission, with robust human rights due diligence and accountability. We will continue to work with Council members and partners to ensure that the international response is effective, coordinated and focused on improving the lives of the Haitian people.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We consistently support the extension of BINUH’s mandate and the strengthening of the United Nations’ work in Haiti on the basis of respect for Haiti’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity. We believe that the primary focus must remain on a Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process, the restoration of democratic institutions, and the improvement of the security situation. At the same time, we stress that the illicit trafficking and diversion of arms and ammunition into Haiti must be addressed effectively, including by the States responsible for arms exports. Humanitarian exemptions under the sanctions regime must be applied in a timely and transparent manner, and the sanctions must not worsen the humanitarian situation. We also proceed from the understanding that the provisions concerning a strategic assessment and any future transition of the international presence do not prejudge any decision by the Council; any transition must be conditions-based, subject to a request from the Government of Haiti and approved by the Security Council.
before.Sierra Leone: Thank you, Mr. President. Sierra Leone will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We reaffirm our strong commitment to Haiti’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and unity. We support the renewal of BINUH’s mandate and an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process leading to credible, free and fair elections. We underscore the urgent need to protect civilians, ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and fully implement the arms embargo and sanctions regime to stop the illicit flow of arms to armed gangs. We also call for predictable and sustained support to the Multinational Security Support mission, with full respect for international human rights law and due diligence, and for accountability for all violations. Sierra Leone stands with the people of Haiti and with regional efforts, including those of CARICOM and the African Union, to restore peace, stability and dignity.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia will vote in favour of the draft resolution before us. We support the extension of BINUH’s mandate as a vital contribution to a Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process, the protection of civilians, accountability for grave violations, and coordinated international support. Slovenia underscores that all efforts must respect Haiti’s sovereignty and international law, ensure the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society, and include robust human rights due diligence and unhindered humanitarian access. We also stress the importance of full implementation of the arms embargo and sanctions regime, as well as predictable and sustainable support for the Multinational Security Support mission, with clear benchmarks and accountability. Slovenia remains committed to working with all Council members and regional partners in support of the Haitian people.
before.Somalia: Thank you, Mr. President. Somalia welcomes the draft resolution and the penholders’ efforts to preserve Council unity on Haiti. We vote in favour because the text renews critical support for BINUH, the MSS mission and the Haitian people in a deeply deteriorating security and humanitarian situation. At the same time, we reiterate our view that the sustainability of the MSS mission requires predictable and sustainable funding. While we welcome the reference to relevant Council decisions, we would have preferred an explicit reference to all available options, including United Nations assessed contributions. We will continue to work with partners to ensure that this issue is addressed in the Council’s future deliberations.
before.United States of America: The United States thanks Panama for its leadership and is proud to co-sponsor this important resolution. The Haitian people continue to endure an unacceptable security and humanitarian crisis, with gangs controlling much of Port-au-Prince and impunity and arms trafficking worsening the suffering. This Council must renew BINUH’s mandate, strengthen coordination with the MSS mission and the Government of Haiti, ensure predictable support for security efforts, and press for a Haitian-led political process leading to credible elections. The United States urges all members to support this text and will vote in favour. We call on all Member States to fully implement the sanctions and arms embargo and to act urgently to protect civilians and deliver humanitarian assistance.

after.China:
China welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH). We thank Panama and the United States for their work as co-penholders. China supports the renewal of BINUH’s mandate because it is conducive to sustaining United Nations good offices, supporting a Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process, and coordinating international assistance to Haiti.

China reaffirms its strong commitment to Haiti’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity. The future of Haiti must be decided by the Haitian people. International support must be provided at the request of and in close consultation with the Government of Haiti and must fully respect Haitian ownership.

The security and humanitarian situation in Haiti remains grave, and China is deeply concerned that arms and ammunition continue to flow into the country, fuelling gang violence and undermining the arms embargo. We call on all Member States, especially arms-exporting States, to earnestly implement resolution 2752 (2024) and the sanctions regime, strengthen border and customs controls, and prevent the illicit trafficking and diversion of arms. Sanctions should be targeted at armed gangs and criminal networks, while humanitarian exemptions must be fully preserved.

China supports BINUH in helping Haiti strengthen the rule of law, protect civilians, promote human rights and prepare for credible elections. We also call for greater efforts to address the root causes of Haiti’s instability, including poverty, underdevelopment and weak state capacity. The international community should provide predictable support to the Multinational Security Support mission and to Haiti’s own capacity-building. China will continue to work with Council members to support the Haitian people in restoring stability, security and development.
after.France:
Monsieur le Président,

La France se félicite de l’adoption à l’unanimité de cette résolution, qui proroge le mandat de la BINUH jusqu’au 15 juillet 2026. Nous remercions Panama et les États-Unis pour leur travail.

La France réaffirme son plein soutien à la souveraineté, à l’indépendance et à l’intégrité territoriale d’Haïti. La priorité demeure une transition politique véritablement haïtienne, inclusive et crédible, conduisant à des élections libres et régulières et au rétablissement des institutions démocratiques. Nous appelons tous les acteurs haïtiens à y œuvrer, avec la pleine participation des femmes, des jeunes et de la société civile.

La protection des civils, l’accès humanitaire sans entrave et la lutte contre l’impunité doivent rester au cœur de notre action. La France appelle à la mise en œuvre pleine et effective du régime de sanctions et de l’embargo sur les armes, y compris par les États exportateurs, afin de tarir les flux illicites vers les gangs. Nous continuons de soutenir la Mission multinationale d’appui à la sécurité et la Police nationale haïtienne.

La France reste mobilisée, avec ses partenaires européens et internationaux, pour répondre à l’urgence humanitaire et accompagner le peuple haïtien vers la stabilité et la démocratie.
after.Guyana:
I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of the three African members of the Security Council, namely Algeria, Sierra Leone and Somalia, as well as my own country, Guyana — the A3+.

The A3+ welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti. We thank Panama and the United States for their constructive efforts as co-penholders and for preserving Council unity at a critical moment for Haiti.

The A3+ voted in favour because we remain deeply concerned by the grave security, humanitarian and human rights situation in Haiti, including the reported control of over 90 per cent of Port-au-Prince by violent gangs, continued massacres, sexual and gender-based violence, attacks on children and humanitarian personnel, displacement and famine-like conditions. We condemn these acts in the strongest terms and stress the need for accountability and justice.

We reaffirm Haiti’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and unity. International support must remain at the request of and in close consultation with the Government and people of Haiti. We support BINUH’s continued good offices and political facilitation for an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process, in close coordination with CARICOM and the African Union, leading to credible, inclusive, free and fair elections and the restoration of democratic institutions, with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society.

We underscore the need for full implementation of the sanctions and arms embargo regimes established by resolution 2653 (2022) and renewed by resolution 2752 (2024). All Member States, in particular arms-exporting States, must take effective measures to prevent the illicit trafficking and diversion of arms and ammunition to Haiti. Humanitarian exemptions and fair and clear procedures must be preserved.

The A3+ also stresses the importance of predictable and sustained support for the Multinational Security Support mission, in close coordination with the Haitian National Police and BINUH, and with robust human rights due diligence and accountability. We call for safe, timely and unhindered humanitarian access and for strengthened protection of civilians, including internally displaced persons and persons in vulnerable situations.

Guyana and the A3+ remain committed to standing with the people of Haiti and to supporting a Haitian-led path towards peace, stability and democratic renewal.
after.Panama:
Mr. President,

Panama thanks all members of the Council for their support and welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution. As penholder, together with the United States, we believe the Council has sent a clear message of unity and sustained commitment to the people of Haiti at a critical moment.

The extension of BINUH’s mandate until 15 July 2026 is essential to continue supporting a Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process, the protection of civilians, humanitarian access, accountability and the restoration of democratic institutions. Panama also stresses the importance of full implementation of the sanctions and arms embargo, including preventing illicit arms trafficking, while preserving humanitarian exemptions and fair and clear procedures.

Panama remains firmly committed to Haiti’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and unity. We call on all Member States, regional organizations and international partners to turn this unanimous decision into concrete action in support of the Haitian people and a credible path toward elections and stability.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Russian Federation: Thank you, Mr. President. The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. We welcome the Council’s unanimous support for extending BINUH’s mandate and for the United Nations’ continued work in Haiti on the basis of respect for Haiti’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity. At the same time, we stress that international assistance must be delivered at the request of and in close coordination with the Government of Haiti. BINUH’s efforts should focus on political facilitation, inclusive national dialogue and preparations for credible elections, rather than duplicating the role of the Multinational Security Support mission. We remain deeply concerned by the humanitarian situation and emphasize that the sanctions and arms embargo must be implemented effectively, above all to stop the illicit flow of arms into Haiti, including from arms-exporting States. Humanitarian exemptions must function in a timely and transparent manner, and the sanctions must not worsen the suffering of the Haitian people. A lasting solution can only be achieved through a Haitian-led political settlement that addresses the root causes of the crisis. The Russian Federation will continue to monitor implementation closely. Thank you.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Thank you, Mr President. The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution and thanks Panama and the United States for their leadership. We are pleased to have voted in favour.

The extension of BINUH’s mandate is vital at a time when over 90 per cent of Port-au-Prince is reportedly under gang control, and when the Haitian people face appalling violence, displacement and famine conditions. We reiterate our strong commitment to Haiti’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and unity.

We support BINUH’s role in providing good offices and political facilitation for an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned process leading to credible, free and fair elections and the restoration of democratic institutions, with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth and civil society. We also stress the importance of protecting civilians, ensuring safe and unhindered humanitarian access, accountability for serious violations, and robust human rights due diligence for all security providers.

The United Kingdom remains a strong supporter of the Multinational Security Support mission and pays tribute to Kenya and all contributing countries. International security support must be predictable and sustainable, and we should continue to consider options for the mission’s transformation in close consultation with Haiti and regional partners.

Full implementation of the arms embargo and sanctions regime is essential. We call on all Member States, in particular arms-exporting States, to take effective measures to prevent the illicit trafficking and diversion of arms and ammunition to Haiti, while preserving humanitarian exemptions and fair and clear procedures.

The United Kingdom will continue to work with Haiti, CARICOM, the United Nations and all partners to support the Haitian people’s path to stability, democracy and recovery. Thank you.
after.United States of America:
Mr. President, the United States welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution renewing BINUH’s mandate. We thank Panama for its partnership and all Council members for their support. This unanimous vote demonstrates the Council’s continued commitment to the people of Haiti and to a Haitian-led, Haitian-owned path out of this crisis.

The United States remains deeply concerned by the deteriorating security and humanitarian situation, including the escalating violence of armed gangs, attacks on civilians, and the illicit trafficking and diversion of arms. This resolution must now be implemented in full. We call on all Member States to enforce the arms embargo and sanctions regime, prevent the diversion of weapons, and hold accountable those who finance and enable gang violence.

BINUH must continue its good offices, human rights monitoring, and coordination with the Multinational Security Support mission, the Government of Haiti, and international partners. We underscore the need for safe, timely and unhindered humanitarian access and for the protection of civilians. The United States supports the Haitian people’s aspirations for stability, democratic institutions, and credible, inclusive elections, and we will continue to work with Haiti, CARICOM, and all partners to advance peace and prosperity. Thank you, Mr. President.
